claims.text: Adding approximately 5 atomic percent aluminum to the baseline high-entropy alloy will improve its mechanical durability.
Adding approximately 5 atomic percent aluminum to the baseline high-entropy alloy will improve its room-temperature creep resistance.
Adding approximately 5 atomic percent aluminum to the baseline high-entropy alloy will improve its corrosion resistance.
Aluminum addition is expected to promote grain refinement in the HEA.
Aluminum addition is expected to form a stable, continuous Al2O3 film on the alloy surface.
A continuous alumina film enhances corrosion resistance by acting as a protective barrier.
The aluminum-induced refined grain structure increases yield strength.
The aluminum-induced refined grain structure reduces room-temperature creep by impeding dislocation motion.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the aluminum-modified alloy should have higher yield strength.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the aluminum-modified alloy should have a lower room-temperature creep rate.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the aluminum-modified alloy should have a lower corrosion current density or corrosion rate in salt-spray or chloride-rich exposure.
The predicted improvements should apply to HEAs similar in composition and processing to those used in aerospace fasteners.
The predicted effect may not generalize to significantly different alloy systems or processing routes.
